The inconclusive result from qwen was solely due to an API error (HTTP 400) preventing it from processing the PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml, not due to any security concerns. data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool failure (HTTP 400 API error) in the qwen model, which prevented it from evaluating the PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml, resulting in an 'inconclusive' verdict. The deepseek model successfully evaluated these files and found them safe.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: Tool errors (e.g., API timeouts or 400 errors) should not trigger an 'inconclusive' package verdict if the failure is transient; the system should retry or fall back to another model.
Escalation triggers should distinguish between genuine security disagreements and tool/infrastructure failures to avoid unnecessary re-audits.
